messages:
james_cust: Hey support — console UI for project `acme-pay` shows region = eu-west1 for recent requests, but our request logs and customer complaints show traffic being served from us-central1 and latency spiked. Example log line: 
```
2024-06-18T14:22:03Z request_id=req_9a3f model=redwood-13b serving_region=us-central1 client_region=eu-west1 latency_ms=420
```
This causes ~350ms extra tail latency for EU users. Can you confirm whether this is a routing/failover issue or a telemetry mismatch? We need a timeline and remediation.

sara_support: Thanks @james_cust — sorry about the impact. Can you paste the full request-id(s) and the API request timestamp range? Also send org id and the last 4 chars of the API key used (we'll only use that for matching). I'll start checking routing traces. :mag_right:

james_cust: Request ids: req_9a3f, req_9b02. Time window: 2024-06-18T14:20:00Z - 2024-06-18T14:25:00Z. Org: acme-pay-prod (org_482). API key ends with `..c4f2`.

sara_support: Got it. Pulling routing traces now. @kai_infra do you see traces for req_9a3f? I suspect a fallback to us-central due to pop capacity, but want to confirm.
kai_infra: Looking. Quick note: console region label is derived from front-end region tag (preferred POP) while serving_region in logs is the actual POP that served the request. They should usually match but can diverge during failover. Querying tracing backend for req_9a3f...
kai_infra: Found routing_events for req_9a3f: initial route=eu-west1, fallback_triggered=true fallback_target=us-central1 fallback_reason=pop_overload at 2024-06-18T14:21:58Z. Also saw a short spike in eu-west1 avail capacity ~14:21:56Z.

ingrid_prod: Adding context from console ingestion: UI badges are updated from a cached mapping that refreshes every ~30s. If a fallback happened quickly it may show preferred region (eu-west1) while logs show actual (us-central1). That mismatch is expected but we should make it clearer in the UI.

sara_support: Ok that's useful. @james_cust — seems routing fallback occurred due to capacity pressure in eu-west1 leading to automatic fallback to us-central1. Two follow-ups: 1) Did you have a hard region pin in the request? 2) Did you have any non-default routing policy?
james_cust: We are not pinning region in requests. Using standard routing with customer-tier=paid. No custom routing policy. We expect EU traffic to stay in eu-west1. Is fallback policy documented?

sara_support: It is — fallback policy is documented in the runbook but we'll paste relevant bits. Short: if pop_util > 95% for X seconds requests may be routed to next compatible POP to preserve latency SLOs. We should still surface it better.

ops_oncall: Paging eng-runtime for full audit and to confirm whether this was due to autoscale delay or a bug in capacity accounting. @ingrid_prod can you attach the autoscaler events and capacity graph for eu-west1 around 14:20-14:23?
ingrid_prod: Attaching snippet from infra metrics (summarized):
```
2024-06-18T14:20:30Z eu-west1 active_hosts=12 util=88%
2024-06-18T14:21:30Z eu-west1 active_hosts=12 util=97%  <-- spike
2024-06-18T14:22:00Z eu-west1 active_hosts=12 util=99%
2024-06-18T14:23:00Z eu-west1 autoscale_trigger=start provisioning_hosts=2 expected_ready=14
2024-06-18T14:25:00Z eu-west1 active_hosts=14 util=62%
```
So autoscaler started after the spike; fallback window matches.

kai_infra: That aligns: fallback window (14:21:58) occurred before new hosts came online. routing_events show fallback due to pop_overload. Also check: we have a bug where console's "primary region" badge is derived from the customer's preferred region metadata not the instant serving region — we should probably change label to "preferred region (may fallback)".
sara_support: For remediation: 1) We'll mark this as expected behavior but poor UX and update docs + console copy. 2) For immediate customer relief we can: enable reserved capacity in eu-west1 for acme-pay (hold 2 hosts) or increase burst priority. Which do you prefer @james_cust?
james_cust: Prefer reserved capacity for EU. Cost ok; need predictable latency for customers in EU. Can you open an order for 2 reserved hosts in eu-west1 and make the change ASAP?
sara_support: Filing request with sales/eng ops. Meanwhile I'll add a dashboard alert to show when fallback events occur per project so you can get alerts next time.

routing-bot: NOTE: routing-events-export for org_482 contains 2 fallback events between 2024-06-18T14:21:58Z and 2024-06-18T14:22:05Z. IDs: req_9a3f, req_9b02.

ops_oncall: Eng-runtime, can you confirm there's no telemetry corruption? The logs show consistent serving_region=us-central1 and the routing-events have explicit fallback_reason=pop_overload. I think this is capacity-induced fallback and a UX mismatch, not misrouted single-request bug.

ingrid_prod: One more subtle thing: we also saw a brief network partition between edge-router eu-west1 and control plane at 14:21:55Z; control-plane couldn't provision ephemeral capacity for ~20s which exacerbated the autoscale delay. We're investigating whether that's an unrelated incident.
kai_infra: Proposed next steps for this thread: 1) Support closes loop with customer and open reserved capacity work item. 2) Product/Console: change UI copy + add time-since-last-fallback badge. 3) Eng-runtime: postmortem on autoscale latency and control-plane partition. 4) Docs: add explicit note about UI vs serving_region mismatch during failover.
sara_support: @james_cust I'll proceed with reserved capacity order and send you an ETA. Also enabling project-level fallback alerts. Apologies again — we'll follow up with timeline and the postmortem link once eng-runtime completes. :handshake:

james_cust: Thanks, appreciate the quick triage. Please keep me posted on ETA, and let me know if you need any more logs or samples.

ops_oncall: Marking thread as escalated-to-runtime. Creating incident tracker: #INC-2024-1725 (routing-fallback-eu-west).
